title: Dynamic exporter orchestrator with failover and synthetic-span enrichment
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: We currently have multiple downstream tracing backends (Tempo for long-term storage, Jaeger for fast query paths) and several OTLP exporter paths. Operators need per-tenant routing, bandwidth-aware fallback, and a small surface to add synthetic metadata to spans so downstream systems can make routing/sampling decisions.

Goal: Build a lightweight orchestration layer in the tracing pipeline (preferably as an OTEL collector extension) that: 1) dynamically selects an exporter target per-tenant based on configured policies (latency SLO, cost budget, tenant tier), 2) transparently fails over to a secondary exporter when the primary is slow or degraded, 3) enriches a small set of spans with synthetic tags (routing_hint, sampling_bucket, tenant_quota) to improve downstream aggregation and billing, and 4) emits operational metrics for SLO compliance and debugging.

Scope: Implement the orchestrator as a new component in the collector pipeline used by hosted and dedicated modes. Support config-driven per-tenant policy rules, on-the-fly policy reloads, and health-check-based failover. Provide integration adapters for Tempo and Jaeger exporters and a generic OTLP sink.

Out of scope: Full UI in Console (we will add a Console card in a follow-up), persistent per-span annotation storage, or deep rewriter for legacy trace tags.

Acceptance criteria:
- Config schema that supports tenant -> [primary, secondary] exporter mapping plus policy primitives (latency_threshold_ms, sampling_override, budget_tokens_per_minute).
- Orchestrator routes >99.9% of spans to primary exporter when healthy and fails over within 250ms of health degradation under load.
- Synthetic tags are injected for at least 3 fields (routing_hint, sampling_bucket, tenant_quota) and are nullable unless policy enables them.
- Unit and integration tests cover exporter selection, failover, and enrichment; e2e test with a small synthetic trace generator validates routing behavior.
- Prometheus metrics emitted: orchestrator_requests_total, orchestrator_failovers_total, orchestrator_primary_latency_ms (histogram), orchestrator_policy_eval_duration_ms.

High-level design notes:
- Placement: collector extension that runs after initial batching and before exporter queueing. This allows us to use collector health and exporter queue metrics for decisions.
- Policy engine: simple rule evaluator with LRU cache keyed by tenant id; policy reload via SIGHUP / API.
- Health checks: use exporter-specific latencies and last-success timestamps; if moving average latency > configured threshold OR consecutive errors > N, mark unhealthy and switch.
- Enrichment: deterministic, minimal mutation of span tags; any enrichment must be opt-in per-tenant to avoid PII leakage.
- Backpressure: when all exporters are degraded, orchestrator should drop non-essential spans based on tenant sampling_override and emit a high-priority alert.

Testing and rollout:
- Unit tests for policy evaluation and enrichment.
- Integration test harness that spins up fake Jaeger and Tempo collectors and asserts routing.
- Canary rollout to a small set of non-critical tenants with verbose logging and auto-rollback if failover rate > 0.5% for 10m.

Observability and dashboards:
- Create a Grafana dashboard showing primary vs secondary routing counts, failover incidents, per-tenant policy hits, and orchestrator latency percentiles.
- Add a Console alert if orchestrator_failovers_total spikes per cluster.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: incorrect enrichment leaks tenant identifiers. Mitigation: enrichment disabled by default and gated behind tenant opt-in flags plus an automated scan for sensitive keys.
- Risk: policy misconfiguration routes heavy tenants to low-cost backends causing latency regressions. Mitigation: default safety caps on bandwidth per exporter and a dry-run mode for policy changes.

Next steps:
1) Finalize config schema (this ticket) and add Confluence spec.
2) Implement initial extension prototype.
3) Add integration tests and dashboards.
4) Canary and iterate.
comments: 2026-01-10 - Ava Chen: Created ticket and drafted goals after ops sync. Linked to observability roadmap. Asked for engineering owners to volunteer for prototype.

2026-01-12 - Rajesh Kumar: Accepted assignment. Initial plan: implement as an OTEL collector extension, reuse existing exporter adapters, add a simple policy DSL. Blocking question about whether Console will surface rules (we'll add Console integration in a follow-up).

2026-01-14 - Design review: Liam O'Connor: Reviewed enrichment fields; requested explicit opt-in and PII checklist. Also requested a way to tag spans as immutable if they originate from customer instrumentation. Action: add tenant opt-in flag and validation.

2026-01-16 - Engineering note: Prototype shows primary->secondary failover triggered reliably when we inject exporter latency; current failure detection window at 30s is too long — lowering to 10s for canary. Perf impact appears negligible on a small test cluster.

2026-01-19 - QA: Ran integration harness against local fake-collectors. Found an edge case where consecutive recoveries flip-flop between exporters under burst; added hysteresis (min_failover_interval_ms) to policy. Tests updated.
2026-01-22 - Rajesh Kumar: PR opened (WIP) for collector extension and test harness. Metrics emitted locally and basic Grafana panels created. Next: security review and canary plan.
